replying_to: Replying to 3D-Scene-Entities: Using Phrase-to-3D-Object Correspondences for Richer Visio-Linguistic Models in 3D Scenes
display_title: Official Review of Paper444 by Reviewer VaCN

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to curate the annotations for associating the 3D corresponding objects with each noun phrase in referential sentences from Nr3D and ScanRefer. Based on the additional annotations, the paper proposes auxiliary losses for both neural listeners and neural speakers on top of state-of-the-art methods. Experiments are conducted on the Nr3D and ScanRefer datasets with ablation study over the proposed auxiliary losses.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- The proposed dataset associates all the nouns in the referential sentences with the 3D object instances in the ScanNet, which acts as an extensive contribution to study in related fields.
- The proposed auxiliary losses, especially the anchor prediction loss and the distractor prediction loss, boost the performance of the neural listening and captioning performance. The ablative experiments also verify the significance of each component.

Weakness:
- The major concern lies in the motivation of the proposed dataset. The additional annotations introduced here mainly involve the ``anchor`` objects in the referential expression. While the direct supervision of object localization (e.g., anchor object prediction) can help the model’s 3D grounding capability, it’s not intuitive to conceptualize the necessity of the proposed dataset under the context of 3D referential expression understanding. In Nr3D and ScanRefer, most referential expressions guarantee the target can be localized unambiguously given the anchor objects. This shows humans don’t need to enumerate all the anchor boxes to locate the target object. 
- Some over-claims. ``a natural and interpretable manner,  i.e.,  by better learning high-order (primarily, spatial) object-to-object relations`` is an over-claim. The high-order relation is not modeled in the current design or the dataset curation. The “Semantic robustness” is also inaccurate as the incorrect predictions in Figure 4 cannot be counted as semantic errors for granted. More in-depth analysis of the error sources should be provided in the discussion.
- It seems the cross-attention map loss is not helping from the ablation study. Any justification for why it’s necessary?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity and Quality: The paper writing is overall easy to follow except for some missing details on the dataset annotation. Some typos: e.g., Page 8 line 1.
Novelty: The major contribution lies in the proposed dataset, and evaluation methods are conducted on top of state-of-the-art models.
Reproducibility: Implementation details are included in the supplementary material.

Some questions:
- Does the annotator find all the 3D boxes for every noun (category-matched) in the referential phrase or the corresponding 3D boxes (instance-matched)?
- For the distractor prediction, will there be no distractor in some cases when “24.3% of all the anchor objects are unique in Nr3D and 39.1% of all anchor objects are unique in ScanRefer”?
content.summary_of_the_review: My ratings are based on my evaluation of my strengths and weaknesses above. The current motivation of the paper is not entirely convincing. From my point of view, the additional annotations/losses introduced are better formulated as the enhancement of the 3D grounding capability for 3D VL models.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work curates a dataset extending from ScanRefer and ReferIt3D for vision-language understanding tasks in the 3D scenes, named 3D Scene Entities (3D-Scent). 3D-Scent provides 4 times more language-to-object correspondences annotations than previous datasets. 3D-Scent is used as additional data for two 3D vision-language tasks, neural listening and neural speaking. A series of auxiliary losses are introduced for adapting the extra annotation about object relation in the 3D-Scent dataset. Equipped with the 3D-Scent and the proposed auxiliary losses, this work improves the SOTA performance by 5.0% in two benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1.	This work complements the richer object-to-object relations expressed in the referential language for the previous 3D vision-language datasets. 
2.	The motivation and the proposed auxiliary losses are technically sound.
3.	The significant performance improvement compared to previous methods verifies the effectiveness of 3D-Scent.

Weakness:
1.	This paper makes little methodological innovative contribution. 
2.	The newly annotated large-scale object-to-object relations are only used on two exsting tasks. 
3.	The limitation is not discussed.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is well-written and clarified but lack of novelty. The new dataset and the code are not released.
content.summary_of_the_review: This work lacks of methodological innovation and thus its contribution is incremental.

display_title: Official Review of Paper444 by Reviewer LqGG

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: Existing studies of combining natural language and 3D scenes show excellent progress. However, they are bottlenecked by a lack of sufficient training data. This work proposed a new 3D-Scent dataset by extending Nr3D and ScanRefer, including extra language-to-object correspondences. The proposed dataset significantly improves the detection accuracy of the sota method detector. It also improves the generalizability of the neural speaker module.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The paper was able to point out the ambiguity and label noise from the existing datasets and tried to improve the annotation by using better UI and hiring professional annotators.
2. Was able to consistently improve the performance of sota methods on Nr3D and ScanRefer datasets. 
3. Using simple, intuitive ways to train models supports the claim that "the new dataset is the most helpful component", not from the loss function tuning. 

Weakness
1. Limited method trained on the new dataset. The paper only reports the experiment results of speaker-listener models. However, other designs exist, i.e., the original ScanRefer baseline. The claim of 3D-Scent is a better dataset to train the model is not yet supported by testing it on variations of models. 
2. Lack of convincing explanations and statistical results to support the claim that "This is a better dataset than existing datasets."
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
About datasets:
1. Stats comparison with Nr3D and ScanRefer: From Fig3 and Tab1, the authors show comparisons of existing datasets. I wish to see an extra column about the new dataset. 
2. What's extended in the dataset exactly: I understand that the dataset has 4x data as the existing datasets, but what exactly is extended? Extra scenes? More objects included? Did you have any methods to explore object-to-object relations? 
3. Why is the new UI a better option? This might not be a question of concern in an ML conference, but your contribution is strongly tied to the annotation quality of 3D-Scent. So I believe it's a fair question to ask. The interface shown in Appendix looks similar to the one from ScanRefer. How does it help the annotation? 

About model training:
1. Excellent work on improving the SOTA model performance using 3D-Scent. However, I would like to know how does 3D-Scent only improves speaker-listener models or if it helps other designs also.
content.summary_of_the_review: My overall recommendation is "3: reject, not good enough". Despite the rejection, I admire the performance improvements of the sota methods. However, the paper lacked justification about why 3D-Scent is a better dataset and didn't show the generalizability of the performance improvements to different methods. Without these detailed analyses of the dataset, no one can assure its quality, even annotated by expensive professional annotators.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
